questions.stem: What is described as the core purpose of Data Governance?
options: Balancing data as an asset with data as a liability
questions.explanation: At its core, Data Governance is about balancing data as an asset with data as a liability, creating clarity, consistency and trust.

questions.stem: Before the era of Big Data, where was Data Governance typically practised?
questions.explanation: Before Big Data, governance was often ignored outside of highly regulated industries.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a component of a Data Governance framework?
questions.explanation: The framework includes strategy, policies, ownership, stewardship, quality, metadata and lineage, privacy, MDM, roles, lifecycle, technology, training and metrics; hardware procurement is not among them.

questions.stem: In a governance framework, what is Data Stewardship?
options: Defining the vision and goals for data
Turning policies into practice on a day-to-day basis
questions.explanation: Data Stewardship is turning policies into practice day to day, and is also named as one of the pillars of governance.

questions.stem: Which governance execution model combines central policies with distributed execution across business units?
questions.explanation: Centralised Governance, Decentralised Execution is the hybrid model with central policies and distributed execution.

questions.stem: In the 'Decentralised – Shared Lists' model, what do business units align on?
options: A single central master data body
Nothing, each unit is fully independent
Shared entities such as customers or vendors, while keeping separate data
questions.explanation: Business units maintain separate data but align on shared entities like customers or vendors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four pillars of Data Governance?
questions.explanation: The pillars are Stewardship, Quality, MDM and Use Cases; encryption belongs under privacy and security components rather than the pillars.

questions.stem: What is the first step in the practical implementation of Data Governance?
questions.explanation: A practical rollout starts by defining roles and responsibilities, then classifying domains, establishing sources, implementing controls and monitoring.

questions.stem: Who is described as the captain of the Data Governance ship?
questions.explanation: The Chief Data Officer (CDO) is the captain, steering between opportunity and risk.

questions.stem: What is the consequence of having no Data Governance, in one phrase?
questions.explanation: 'No Data Governance is equal to Data Swamp' — without governance, organisations do not build a lake, they create a swamp.
